chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Alawi (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: My grandfather narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Hasan ibn Muhammad and Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Rafi' narrated to us, saying: My father informed me about an elder from the Ansar who traced it back to Zaynab bint Abi Rafi', from her mother, who said: Fatimah (peace be upon her) said: 'O Messenger of God, these are your sons, so grant them something.' The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'As for al-Hasan, I granted him my majesty and mastery, and as for al-Husayn, I granted him my generosity and bravery.'
ai.seo_question: What specific virtues did the Prophet Muhammad bestow upon Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Fatimah (peace be upon her) requests the Prophet to bestow specific virtues upon his grandsons, to which he responds by attributing his own divine qualities to them: majesty and pre-eminence for Hasan, and generosity and bravery for Husayn. This hadith is significant in Shia scholarship as it establishes the spiritual and moral inheritance (*warathah*) of the Ahl al-Bayt, illustrating how the Imams embody the essential characteristics of the Prophet Muhammad. It underscores the concept of *tawassul* through the Imams, who serve as the living manifestations of the Prophet's attributes in the post-prophetic era.
